item.title: Europe’s sleepwalking leaders, mercurial Trump, pragmatic US, UN Reform — with Dmitry Polyanskiy
item.description: Olga Bataman and Tara Reade welcome Ambassador Dmitry Polyanskiy, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE, for the Russian perspective on the risk of a direct conflict with Europe, America’s role in the peace talks, and the future of the United Nations. Is Europe sleepwalking into a direct conflict with Russia? Why does Ambassador Polyanskiy say Europe has inched closer to one, and that a single incident could be enough to trigger it? And why does he argue that unpopular European leaders stay in power while leading their populations toward confrontation? Is Washington a mediator or a source of pressure? Why does Ambassador Polyanskiy call Trump “mercurial” while describing US interests as “pragmatic” ? How does he read the mixed signals — peace talks, a sanctions bill headed for Trump’s signature and a planned US base in Poland — and why does he say Russia is not counting on America’s help? And why does he say Europe and Zelensky are trying to derail the understandings reached in Anchorage? Is there a way back? Why does he say Russia’s door to diplomacy remains open, and that the first step is a clear declaration that neither side plans to attack the other? What would a European security “equation” built together with Russia look like — and can Europe move away from a zero-sum approach toward peaceful coexistence? And is the UN slowly dying – or, as Ambassador Polyanskiy argues, are Western countries holding Security Council reform “hostage” ?

item.title: UK detains human rights lawyer, NATO’s somber summit & ‘Op Barbarossa 2.0’ – with Daniel Kovalik
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome human rights lawyer and peace activist Dan Kovalik to recount his recent high-stakes detention at the UK border and discuss the broader geopolitical climate surrounding NATO, Russia, Iran, and the US. Why are Western authorities weaponizing broad anti-terrorism laws against prominent anti-war voices and legal advocates? What does it mean for civil liberties when governments can confiscate electronic devices and collect DNA? We look at the broader geopolitical fallout surrounding the US 250th anniversary, the recent Trump-Putin phone call, and NATO expanding military spending. Daniel also explains why he believes the conflict in Ukraine is already a direct confrontation between Russia and the West – describing it as “Operation Barbarossa 2.0.” Is this historical comparison a warning about where current policies are leading?

item.title: Trump’s changed, Iran and Ukraine as forever wars, midterms don’t matter – with Jimmy Dore
item.description: Olga Bataman and Tara Reade are joined by political commentator Jimmy Dore to talk about Trump’s new hair and new term, Ukraine negotiations, Iran, the current state of the US military, the Charlie Kirk assassination, the Epstein files, and much more. Is the US stretched too thin to win two wars at once? Dore argues the Iran conflict drained missile stockpiles meant for Ukraine – so what does that say about America’s real military capacity, and who might be watching closely? Does it actually matter who wins the US midterms? Dore says no, arguing both parties answer to the same donors regardless of outcome. Is voting still a real lever for change? What really shifted Trump between his first and second terms? Dore lays out a theory involving lawsuits, imprisoned allies, and the Epstein files – and on the ground, how much of the anger Tara found in the US is about foreign policy versus the cost of living?

item.title: Starmer’s out, Poland’s rift with Ukraine & war-2030 – with Mario Bojic
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome Mario Bojic, journalist and anchor of Mario ZNA, to break down the political turbulence shaking Europe, growing tensions between Brussels and Washington, and the changing balance of power in a multipolar world. Is Larry the Cat the only permanent fixture left in Downing Street? We dismantle Keir Starmer’s sudden resignation and the domestic crises pushing the UK to the brink. Is the “Zelensky Curse” a proven pattern for Western leaders who prioritize foreign warmongering over their own citizens? How long can European establishments blame their economic and migration failures on a manufactured external threat? What is driving the growing rift between Ukraine and some of its strongest supporters, including Poland? Has Zelensky become a political liability for leaders who once stood firmly behind him? And are we witnessing the beginning of a broader realignment inside Europe — and the world?

item.title: Weaponized tariffs and why China was ready, Beijing in Iran war, Brzezinski’s nightmare – with Nelson Wong
item.description: Olga and Tara are joined by Nelson Wong, vice chairman and president at the Shanghai Centre for RimPac Strategic and International Studies. We’ll discuss the detention of American human rights lawyer Dan Kovalik in the UK, explore the strategic consequences of the Iran war, Trump’s comments on communism, technological competition, and whether fear – not strength – is driving today’s geopolitical decisions. Was Brzezinski’s “worst nightmare” always destined to become reality? Did the strategic partnership between China, Russia, and Iran emerge despite Western expectations – or because of them? And why does Nelson Wong argue that China spent more than a decade preparing for today’s tariff and trade confrontation with the United States? How vulnerable is China to instability in the Strait of Hormuz? What role does Iranian oil play in China’s long-term strategy, and why does Nelson Wong believe Beijing has already prepared for worst-case scenarios? Can a superpower exist without seeking military dominance? What does China’s leadership believe a global power should look like, and why does Wong reject the idea that every country wants to follow the American model?

item.title: Ukraine’s vanishing men, Trump’s Jimmy Carter problem, stalling peace deals – with Ben Swann
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome investigative journalist Ben Swann – creator of the acclaimed Zelensky Unmasked series – for a wide-ranging conversation on the war in Ukraine that is draining a generation, Trump’s risk of becoming another Jimmy Carter, schisms within US intelligence agencies, Russia’s recent elections, and much more. Is Ukraine’s male population being sent to the front against its will, and why has fighting shifted almost entirely to drones? Why does Swann argue that the war is being run less from the Pentagon and more from the CIA – and what does that mean for who actually controls US policy? Why does Swann call the latest Russia sanctions bill “toothless,” and what does he think it reveals about Washington’s real priorities? Is Trump boxed in by agencies and allies he underestimated? What drove Trump’s decision to strike Iran despite warnings from his own Joint Chiefs chairman and Tulsi Gabbard – and why didn’t it go as planned? What do competing factions within the CIA and other intelligence agencies mean for Trump’s ability to change course?

item.title: Tucker Carlson: US-Israel intel merger is treason, US already at war with Russia, Europe can’t fight
item.description: Renowned journalist Tucker Carlson joins Olga and Tara for a wide-ranging conversation on the future of American foreign policy, the war in Ukraine, US-Russia relations, Israel, Iran, free speech, and the shifting global balance of power. Is the US already in direct conflict with Russia? Why does Tucker argue that the US has lost its sovereignty, and who does he believe is shaping foreign policy decisions? We also discuss the growing tensions between Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu, the prospect of a third political party in the US, and whether the current political system still represents ordinary Americans. Can Europe avoid a direct confrontation with Russia and where is the boundary between proxy support and direct warfare? Are we witnessing a historical pivot of power from West to East, and can global stability survive the shift? We also examine sanctions, energy security, NATO, and the future of diplomacy.
